speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You are presenting with double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness; to begin our investigation, please describe exactly where you see the double vision and if your symptoms worsen when you look up?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The combination of binocular diplopia triggered by looking up/down, proximal muscle weakness worsening with activity and improving with rest, and the absence of sensory deficits or cranial nerve palsy beyond ocular involvement is highly characteristic of Myasthenia Gravis. Please proceed to DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis.
